title: Genuine question about AI-assisted game dev: Why is the pushback so strong when a human is still driving the project?
author: WideWealth7349
selftext:
I've been working on a game for the past 4 weeks using Claude to help with parts of the code. Recently I shared a clip looking for constructive feedback to improve and most of the reaction was just instant dismissal because AI was involved rather than actual feedback on the gameplay.  
I completely understand why low effort AI asset flips get criticized. At the same time you obviously can't just prompt make me a game and publish it. You still have to understand architecture, fix bugs, balance systems and connect everything so the game actually feels coherent and has soul. That still depends 100% on the person behind the project.  
With major studios integrating AI into their tooling right now it feels like the role of a system integrator who holds the vision and brings the pieces together is becoming just as important as writing every line of code manually.  
For those who are strongly against AI tools in indie dev I'd genuinely like to understand the core issue from your perspective. Is it mainly concern about job displacement and years of learned skills being automated or is it more about quality and copyright concerns?

At the end of the day most players just care if a game is fun and runs well. I hope this post works better for a real discussion. I'm not trying to put anyone down here I just want a calm honest conversation about using AI in game dev. Let's keep this respectful and constructive so we can actually have a good discussion
